title: Cardinal Filtration Co. — Final Returns Summary
summary: Final returns summary workbook for Cardinal Filtration Co. (Atlas Crossing Partners Fund I). Exit closed September 20, 2019 via strategic sale to Donaldson Company (NYSE: DCI). The fund held Cardinal for ~5 years (Sept 2014–Sept 2019), completing 4 bolt-on acquisitions (Phoenix Industrial, Apex Filter, Filtration Pros, EnvioGuard). Entry EV of $175M at 7.5x EBITDA; exit EV of $560M at 9.5x EBITDA. Gross MOIC of 3.2x and Gross IRR of 26.1%. Revenue grew from $186M at entry to $472M at exit; Adj. EBITDA from $23.3M to $58.9M. Value creation driven primarily by bolt-on acquisitions ($98M equity contribution), organic growth ($72M), and multiple expansion ($70M).

growth_drivers: Bolt-on acquisitions (4 deals: Phoenix Industrial, Apex Filter, Filtration Pros, EnvioGuard)
Organic revenue growth and margin expansion
Multiple expansion (7.5x to 9.5x)
Distribution center footprint growth (4 to 12 centers)
Customer base growth (3,400 to 11,200 customers)
risks: Private-label mix growth (9% to 28%)
Integration risk across 4 bolt-on acquisitions
Leverage increase (net debt $127M to $185M)

title: Investment Committee Memorandum — Initial Investment Recommendation: Cardinal Filtration Co.
summary: Atlas Crossing Partners Fund I entry IC memo recommending the acquisition of Cardinal Filtration Co., a regional industrial filtration distributor headquartered in Akron, OH, at an enterprise value of $175M (7.5x LTM Adj. EBITDA of $23.3M). The investment thesis centers on a disciplined roll-up strategy in the highly fragmented ~$8B US industrial filtration distribution market, private-label penetration expansion (9% → 25%), supplier consolidation, and organic revenue growth in defensive end markets. The base case underwrites 4 bolt-on acquisitions over a 5-year hold, targeting exit EBITDA of $52M at an 8.5x multiple ($442M EV), implying a 4.0x MOIC and 32% gross IRR. Deal team: S. Kowalski (MD), R. Patel (Principal), L. Chen (VP).

key_quotes.quote: We see a clear path to 2.5–3.5x MOIC over a 5-year hold through a disciplined roll-up strategy in a highly fragmented category, alongside operational improvements in private-label penetration and supplier consolidation.

The $8B US industrial filtration distribution market is served by ~600 sub-$50M-revenue regional distributors. Top 10 hold less than 20% share. We have line-of-sight on 12–15 attractive bolt-on targets within Cardinal's strike zone.

Cardinal currently sells 91% branded product (Donaldson, Parker, 3M, etc.). Top-quartile peers operate at 25–35% private label. Migration over 3 years to 25% PL implies +280bps gross margin expansion (vs. 31.5% LTM).

70% of revenue serves regulated or essential industries (water treatment, power gen, F&B manufacturing). Filtration is a consumable that gets replaced regardless of macro cycles. Stress-tested through 2008–09 downturn: revenue declined just 6% peak-to-trough.

Outreach to 14 prioritized targets; 9 returned signed NDAs and provided initial financials. 5 Tier 1 targets have indicated openness to a transaction at 5.0–5.5x EBITDA on combined revenue of $95M. Three of the five owners are >65 years old with no clear succession plan.

growth_drivers: Roll-up of 12–15 fragmented regional bolt-on targets
Private-label penetration expansion from 9% to 25% (200–400bps GM uplift)
Supplier consolidation from 47 to top-10 suppliers (80–120bps GM savings)
Organic revenue growth in water treatment and F&B end markets
Recurring/contracted revenue model with 87% repeat-revenue share
SG&A leverage via centralized purchasing, IT modernization, DC network optimization
risks: Roll-up integration execution risk
Supplier concentration (top 5 = 38% of spend)
Asian import competition in commodity filtration SKUs
Donaldson/Parker direct-to-customer pressure on large accounts
Industrial cycle exposure (mitigated by 70% defensive end-market mix)
Working capital intensity (71-day cycle)

title: Exit Recommendation — Cardinal Filtration Co.
summary: Atlas Crossing Partners Fund I IC exit memo recommending the sale of Cardinal Filtration Co. to Donaldson Company, Inc. (NYSE: DCI) for $560M enterprise value (9.5x LTM Adj. EBITDA of $58.9M). The deal represents a 5.3-year hold from September 2014, delivering 3.2x gross MOIC and ~26.1% gross IRR (2.6x / 21.2% net). Entry thesis centered on industrial filtration roll-up was largely delivered: 4 bolt-ons completed, gross margin expanded 320bps, private-label penetration grew from 9% to 28%, and revenue scaled from $186M to $472M. Operating margin was flat (thesis miss due to bolt-on mix shift). Sale process run by Baird yielded three final bids; Donaldson selected at $560M all-cash, no financing condition.

key_quotes.quote: Returns: 3.2x gross MOIC and ~26% gross IRR — top-quartile outcome and the highest absolute proceeds in Fund I.

Cardinal is at peak scale relative to standalone optionality. Further organic growth requires geographic expansion into the West and Southeast, where additional capital deployment ($60M+) and integration complexity would extend the hold by 2–3 years.
key_quotes.topic: Why now — strategic rationale for timing

key_quotes.quote: Marketing was structured around Cardinal's scarcity value as a $470M-revenue industrial filtration platform with 12 distribution centers and a successful 5-acquisition rollup track record.
Operating margin: +200bps over hold [plan] — Flat (Y/Y; mix shift from bolt-ons) — Miss — mix effect.
Selected Donaldson — strategic, all-cash, willing to drop financing condition, and providing material premium for product-line complementarity and manufacturing synergies.

growth_drivers: Roll-up M&A strategy (4 bolt-on acquisitions over hold)
Private-label penetration growth from 9% to 28%
Geographic expansion: 4 to 12 distribution centers
Customer base growth from 3,400 to 11,200
Multiple expansion from 7.5x to 9.5x
Strategic buyer premium from Donaldson for product-line complementarity
risks: Operating margin flat vs. +200bps thesis (mix shift from bolt-ons)
EnvioGuard synergies still in progress at exit
Further organic growth would require $60M+ additional capital and 2-3 year hold extension

title: Cardinal Filtration Co. — Final Round Bid Comparison
summary: Final round bid comparison for the exit sale of Cardinal Filtration Co., prepared by ACP/Baird in August 2019. Three bids were received: Donaldson (DCI) at $560M EV (9.5x LTM EBITDA, 100% cash, no financing condition) was selected as the highest value and highest certainty bid; Parker (Strategic B) at $530M (9.0x) was the runner-up; and Sponsor X (PE) at $520M (8.8x, with earnout and management rollover requirements) was declined. title: Cardinal Filtration Co. — Management Presentation
summary: Management presentation prepared for final-round buyer meetings in June–July 2019 as part of Cardinal Filtration Co.'s exit process. Cardinal is a national industrial filtration products distributor headquartered in Akron, OH, founded in 1987 and acquired by Atlas Crossing Partners in September 2014. Over the ~5-year hold, the company grew revenue from $186M to $472M LTM through organic growth and four bolt-on acquisitions, with EBITDA expanding from $23.3M to $58.9M. Key value creation levers include a disciplined roll-up M&A playbook, private-label (CardinalGuard) expansion from 9% to 28% of revenue with a 600bps GM premium, and geographic DC footprint growth from 4 to 12 locations. Future opportunities highlighted include further geographic expansion, private-label penetration to 35–40%, engineered solutions/service revenue growth, and a potential Canadian distribution hub.

growth_drivers: Roll-up M&A of regional distributors at 5–6x pre-synergy EBITDA with rapid purchasing integration
CardinalGuard private-label expansion: 9% → 28% of revenue, targeting 35–40% penetration
Geographic expansion into Pacific Northwest, Mountain West, and Mid-Atlantic via new DCs
Engineered solutions / service revenue growth from 9% toward 15–18% of revenue mix
International distribution opportunity via Toronto DC serving Canadian customers
risks: Integration risk from four bolt-on acquisitions and ongoing M&A playbook
Private-label concentration risk and dependency on CardinalGuard margin premium
Founder/family dynamic with CEO Steve Brandt (founder's son, 32-year tenure)

title: Cardinal Filtration Co. — Closing Checklist
summary: Closing checklist for the sale of Cardinal Filtration Co. to Donaldson, managed by Kirkland & Ellis LLP on behalf of ACP, targeting a close of September 20, 2019. All 20 line items are marked complete. Key milestones include execution of the Stock Purchase Agreement (Aug 21), HSR early termination (Sep 5), lien releases from Madison Capital, R&W insurance binding ($28M limit), and closing wire of $560M purchase price on Sep 20. Debt payoff to Madison Capital totaled $185M; net equity proceeds to ACP Fund I were $190M; $20M placed in indemnity escrow; and $221M total LP distribution (including 2017 recap) was issued Sep 23 and distributed Sep 27. Transaction expenses totaled ~$15M (Baird $11.2M, K&E $2.8M, other $1.0M).

title: Cardinal Filtration Co. — Funds Flow Memorandum
summary: Closing funds flow memorandum prepared by Kirkland & Ellis LLP for the sale of Cardinal Filtration Co. to Donaldson Company on September 20, 2019. Enterprise value agreed at $560M. After repaying $185.4M of Madison Capital debt, $15M in transaction expenses, and a $20M indemnity escrow holdback, net equity proceeds to ACP Fund I totaled ~$339.6M. The equity waterfall shows return of $69M invested capital (platform + 4 bolt-ons), an 8% preferred return hurdle of $47.2M, and remaining carry split 80/20 between LPs ($178.7M) and GP ($44.7M). Combined with a 2017 dividend recap LP share of $27.9M, cumulative LP proceeds total $323.8M.

title: Cardinal Filtration Co. — HSR Filing Summary
summary: HSR Filing Summary prepared by Kirkland & Ellis LLP for the acquisition of Cardinal Filtration Co. by Donaldson Company, Inc. at a transaction value of $560M. The filing was made on August 22, 2019; early termination of the 30-day waiting period was granted by the DOJ Antitrust Division on September 5, 2019 (Day 14), with the transaction closing on September 20, 2019. Clearance was granted on the basis of no competitive overlap — Donaldson is a manufacturer and Cardinal is a distributor, presenting a vertical rather than horizontal combination with minimal antitrust risk.

key_quotes.quote: No competitive overlap identified — Donaldson is a manufacturer; Cardinal is a distributor
The vertical integration (manufacturer acquires distributor) presents limited horizontal overlap and no market concentration concerns under either HHI or unilateral effects analysis.
Early termination of waiting period granted by DOJ Antitrust Division — September 5, 2019 (Day 14)

risks: Regulatory/antitrust review (HSR reportable transaction)

title: Cardinal Filtration Co. — Sell-Side Quality of Earnings Summary
summary: Grant Thornton Transaction Advisory Services prepared this sell-side Quality of Earnings (VDD QofE) for Cardinal Filtration Co. on behalf of Atlas Crossing Partners (ACP) in support of the May 2019 exit/sale process. The report bridges LTM March 2019 reported EBITDA of $52.4M to a preliminary adjusted EBITDA of $58.9M through $6.5M in addbacks (CEO comp normalization, EnvioGuard integration costs, non-recurring legal/advisory, phantom equity amortization, D&A reclassification) offset by a $0.6M revenue timing haircut. Key findings confirm high revenue quality (87% recurring, no customer >6% of revenue), supportable and well-documented adjustments, normalized working capital (NWC peg of $66M), and a structural private-label margin premium for the CardinalGuard product line (40.8% GM vs. 34.3% branded).

key_quotes.quote: 87% of LTM revenue is from accounts with >2-year tenure. Top 50 customers represent 47% of revenue; all 50 have been customers for >5 years. No single customer exceeds 6% of revenue.
Total addbacks of $6.5M against reported EBITDA of $52.4M are well-documented. The EnvioGuard integration costs ($2.8M) are evidenced by third-party invoices and internal project tracking.

CardinalGuard gross margin of 40.8% vs. 34.3% for branded — a 650bps premium. Margin advantage is structural: proprietary specifications, single-source manufacturing agreements, and customer-spec lock-in.
NWC as % of revenue has been stable at 14.2–14.8% over FY17–LTM. Proposed NWC peg of $66M reflects trailing-12-month average.

growth_drivers: High recurring revenue base (87% of LTM revenue from accounts with >2-year tenure)
No single customer exceeds 6% of revenue — diversified customer base
CardinalGuard private-label gross margin premium of 650bps vs. branded (40.8% vs. 34.3%)
Structural private-label advantage via proprietary specs, single-source manufacturing, and customer-spec lock-in
risks: Q1 2019 customer prepayment (pull-forward revenue) — $0.6M non-recurring benefit reversed
EnvioGuard acquisition caused temporary NWC spike of ~$3M (now normalized)
Phantom equity settled at exit — one-time cash outflow

title: Project Titan — Confidential Information Memorandum
summary: CIM prepared by Robert W. Baird & Co. on behalf of Atlas Crossing Partners Fund I for the sale of Cardinal Filtration Co. ("Project Titan"). Cardinal is a national industrial filtration products distributor headquartered in Akron, OH, serving 11,200 customers across manufacturing, power generation, water treatment, F&B, and HVAC. ACP acquired the business in 2014 at ~$186M revenue and grew it to $472M LTM revenue / $58.9M Adj. EBITDA through four bolt-on acquisitions, private-label expansion (CardinalGuard now 28% of revenue), and supplier consolidation across 12 distribution centers. The process is a targeted sell-side with IOI deadline June 14, 2019 and anticipated close September 20, 2019. Strategic rationale for a buyer centers on cross-sell into Cardinal's 11,200 mid-market accounts and continued private-label penetration toward 35–40%.

key_quotes.quote: Cardinal has grown from a single-location, $186M-revenue business at ACP's entry in 2014 to a 12-distribution-center national platform generating $472M in LTM revenue and $58.9M in Adj. EBITDA through disciplined roll-up M&A, private-label expansion, and supplier consolidation.
Cardinal's proprietary product line (CardinalGuard) grew from 9% of revenue in 2014 to 28% in LTM 2019, carrying a 600bps gross margin premium vs. branded products.
4 bolt-ons acquired at average 5.5x pre-synergy / 3.9x post-synergy EBITDA multiple. Each acquisition was fully integrated within 18 months.
Industrial filtration is a consumable — maintenance schedules are driven by regulatory compliance and equipment warranty requirements, not capex cycles.
Average customer tenure of 11.4 years reflects structural lock-in from technical service and engineered-solutions relationships.

growth_drivers: Roll-up M&A playbook — 4 bolt-ons acquired at avg. 5.5x pre-synergy / 3.9x post-synergy EBITDA
Private-label expansion: CardinalGuard grew from 9% to 28% of revenue, carrying 600bps GM premium
National distribution platform (12 DCs, 2-day delivery to >90% of customers)
Defensive, essential end-market exposure (70% regulated/essential industries)
Supplier consolidation driving 80–120bps gross margin uplift on acquired businesses
risks: LTM EBITDA margin (12.5%) has not recovered to FY16 peak (13.9%), suggesting some margin pressure
Most recent bolt-on (EnvioGuard, Mar 2018) still integrating — synergies in progress
Private-label penetration (28%) below best-in-class peers (35–40%), dependent on continued execution
Customer concentration risk not disclosed; 11,200 customers but top-account mix unknown

title: Cardinal Filtration Co. — Escrow Agreement Summary
summary: Post-exit escrow agreement summary for Cardinal Filtration Co. documenting a $20M indemnity holdback (3.57% of EV, implying ~$560M total EV) held by Wells Fargo Bank under the SPA between ACP Fund I (Seller) and Donaldson Company (Buyer). The 18-month escrow was funded at closing on September 20, 2019 and released in full on March 20, 2021 with $412K in accrued interest ($20.412M total), as no indemnification claims were received. An AIG R&W insurance policy ($28M limit, $1.4M premium) was bound concurrently. Governing law is Delaware with JAMS arbitration.

key_quotes.quote: No indemnification claims were received during the 18-month escrow period (September 2019 – March 2021). The escrow was released in full to ACP Fund I on March 20, 2021, plus $412,000 in accrued interest ($20,412,000 total).
$20,000,000 (escrow amount); no above-escrow seller exposure (R&W insurer takes over).
